title: Woman left in Philippines after WWII gets Japan passport, eyes visit

blocks.text: A 90-year-old Japanese-Filipino woman who regained her Japanese nationality this year received a passport at the Japanese Embassy in Manila on Friday, saying she hopes to visit her father’s hometown as early as December. Adelaida Kakazu remained in the Philippines after being separated from her Okinawa-born father following World War II. She expressed a desire to visit his grave and “tell him everything that happened from the time he left us in 1946, when I was 10 years old.” “Please enjoy meeting your family in Okinawa,” Consul General Maya Hamada said as she handed Kakazu her Japanese passport.
